added: packages/runtimes (@sos-2/runtimes): the runtime contract — typed RuntimeDescriptor (id, kind from the typed 5-kind vocabulary, version, capabilities = the DECLARED operation names, typed constraints: MAX_DURATION_MS/MAX_MEMORY_MB/MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES/NETWORK_ACCESS/FILESYSTEM_ACCESS) validated loudly (duplicate capabilities, malformed constraints, UNKNOWN context dimensions all rejected), plus runtimeMatchesContext/selectRuntimesForContext — platform behavior is Context/Adapter data over REGISTERED @sos-2/context dimensions (typed matching per dimension value type: text/enum equality, number, boolean, string-list membership)

the RuntimeHost contract + InMemoryRuntimeHost: executes DECLARED operations against DECLARED runtimes — registerRuntime validates the descriptor and REQUIRES a handler for every declared capability (a runtime claiming an operation it cannot serve is a contract violation); execution order is shape validation -> AUTHORITY GATE -> runtime/operation declaration checks -> run -> observation; the MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES constraint is enforced deterministically over the canonical output size (no hidden clocks anywhere: windows and evaluation points are caller-supplied)

EXECUTION IS AUTHORITY CHECKED: every ExecutionRequest carries a grant reference resolved from the operator-supplied pool and validated through @sos-2/authority's evaluateGrant BEFORE running — expired/revoked grants yield EXECUTION_DENIED with a structured reason { code: GRANT_EXPIRED|GRANT_REVOKED, grant_ref, reason }; a forged request without a grant reference is denied GRANT_MISSING; an unknown grant is denied GRANT_UNKNOWN; the operation provably never runs on denial (no observation, no trace link; pinned by run-flag probes); unknown runtimes, undeclared operations and malformed requests fail LOUDLY (RuntimeError/RuntimeRequestError) — contract violations, not operational denials

RuntimeObservation: the typed, evidence-shaped record of one execution (truthful availability from the frozen 6 states — SUCCESS when the operation returned, FAILURE when it threw or its output was unusable; output/error/window/producer; grant_ref; subject_ref; observed_system_state; OBSERVES/VERIFIES trace_links) — observations are deliberately NOT spine artifacts (the @sos-2/telemetry RawObservation precedent: pre-semantic input) and carry a deterministic 64-hex content-hash id; toRawObservation bridges them into @sos-2/telemetry RawObservations so the merged evidence layer (ingestObservation) mints evidence with VERBATIM availability (pinned for all 6 states)

RUNTIME FEEDS SYSTEM STATE AND EVIDENCE: executions observing a SystemState revision mint OBSERVES (or VERIFIES) trace links through the spine's createTraceLink (source = executed subject, target = observed SystemState id, provenance = runtime/operation/grant) stored in the host's spine TraceLinkStore — the (subject, state, type) relationship is stored once while every observation carries its minted link; runtime observations NEVER mutate System State directly (they are input to reconciliation): the observation carries the SystemState REFERENCE only and the host exposes no system-state write path (pinned by tests: a W2 SystemState artifact is bit-identical before and after executions observing it)
preserved_invariants: expired and revoked grants never authorize (the W1 invariant): the RuntimeHost consumes @sos-2/authority's evaluateGrant verbatim — dead grants yield structured EXECUTION_DENIED denials and the operation never runs (pinned by negative tests with run-flag probes for GRANT_MISSING/GRANT_UNKNOWN/GRANT_EXPIRED/GRANT_REVOKED)

the Semantic Spine remains the ONLY identity/envelope/kind/trace/serialization authority: trace links are minted through the spine's createTraceLink and stored in the spine's TraceLinkStore; observation ids are spine-serializer content hashes; observations reference SystemState revisions by spine id and introduce no new artifact kinds, no envelope shapes and no trace types

runtime observations never mutate System State directly (the W12 acceptance): they are input to reconciliation — pinned by tests proving a W2 SystemState artifact's content hash and envelope are bit-identical after executions observing it, and that the observation carries only the revision reference

platforms and vendors are adapters or contexts — they do not redefine SOS semantics (spec/architecture.md section 17): platform/runtime specifics live in typed context dimensions consumed from @sos-2/context (runtimeMatchesContext), and the execution path never reads context — there is no semantic branch on platform anywhere (the request type structurally cannot carry context)

unknown, failed, unavailable and unsupported remain distinct (spec/architecture.md section 18 / R21): observations carry truthful availability from the frozen 6 states verbatim; a thrown operation is FAILURE with the error preserved, a returned operation is SUCCESS, and the bridge to evidence preserves the state exactly (pinned for all 6 states through ingestObservation)

no frozen contract in spec/contracts/ was modified; spec/, docs/, root files and sibling-owned paths are untouched — all changes are additive under the owned path packages/runtimes (the W12 owned-path contract)
boundary_changes: one new workspace package: @sos-2/runtimes (runtime deps @sos-2/semantic-spine, @sos-2/provenance, @sos-2/telemetry, @sos-2/authority, @sos-2/context; dev-only deps @sos-2/evidence and @sos-2/system-state used by the bridge and no-mutation tests) — one-directional and acyclic

the RuntimeKind and RuntimeConstraintKind vocabularies are NEW typed adapter-plane vocabularies (substrate kinds and resource bounds), not redefinitions of any frozen contract vocabulary; runtime descriptors are deliberately NOT spine artifacts (a runtime is adapter plane) and introduce no second semantic registry
the structured denial codes (GRANT_MISSING, GRANT_UNKNOWN, GRANT_EXPIRED, GRANT_REVOKED) are operational metadata of the authority gate, mirroring the W1 evaluation outcomes one-to-one
